_note: Townsfolk roles, handled as groups. time_kinds = how a step of each task (or activity: flee, fight, heal, patrol, shadow, drill) counts toward the Your people bar: work (their own job), fallback (something else useful), idle or down (fleeing or healing); tasks not listed (a seer) are not counted; workers count by day only (sim/folk_ai.gd _note_time). busy_words = the dawn card word from the share of the round spent in kinds: Stretched (idle share under stretched_below, or for warriors fighting and healing over stretched_above: another would earn their keep), Slack (idle over slack_above, or fighting under slack_below) and Busy between (People.busy_word). They do their job on their own; you only choose who joins at dawn. tags describe the role; fighter = stands and fights, and counts toward the town's power level (sim/power.gd). leanings (optional): a role's dawn cards come with a leaning, rolled when the card is dealt from those whose age (if any) the town has reached; the newcomer still gathers anything, but scores trips for its goods leaning_weight times higher (sim/folk_ai.gd plan_trip). leaning_cards: how many cards of that role, each with a different leaning, go into the dawn pool. Newcomers from family cards and the town's first people have no leaning. warriors: their patrol walks round the town's edge, patrol_margin past the outermost building of the town proper in each of patrol_bins slices of the circle (the first two rings count, and a further ring only where the ring inside it has a building nearby, so far-out fields and huts past an empty ring are left outside; sim/town.gd patrol_radius); once at least from warriors patrol (not shadowing) they walk it in groups of size (patrol_groups, the largest tier reached counts), spread evenly round the town, partners patrol_spacing apart; however near the patrol runs, warriors go for foes up to patrol_watch + 60 from the hearth; by day the first shadow_share of them each shadow a gatherer working past the houses, at most shadow_reach from the hearth (sim/folk_ai.gd _warrior_tick); a gatherer whose warrior is within escort_reach walks escort_speed faster (0.12 = 12%) while no foe is within escort_safe, shown by an escort_color diamond at its feet (FolkAI._note_escorts). By day each drilling hero whose class teaches a mark (data/heroes.json) takes up to pupils_per_hero patrolling warriors without one as drill partners; after mark_seconds of drilling (faster with a teach_mult trait) a warrior earns the mark for good (data/marks.json). build_rate = how fast it raises buildings (tribespeople only help when they have nothing worth fetching). band_tiers: when at least size living townsfolk of a role share a leaning they are a band, and on trips for their leaning's goods each carries carry more and gathers gather_mult faster (0.5 = 50% faster); the highest tier reached counts, not the sum (sim/folk_ai.gd band_tier). rarity (data/rarity.json): the colour of the role's dawn cards (white if none).

tribesperson.name: Tribesperson
tribesperson.text: Gathers food, fuel, wood and stone, and patches the hearth. With nothing worth fetching, lends a hand at a building that suits its leaning or helps raise one. Weak: must be protected.

forager.name: Forager
forager.text: Would rather pick berries and bring food home.

woodcutter.name: Woodcutter
woodcutter.text: Would rather fell timber and bring wood home.

quarrier.name: Quarrier
quarrier.text: Would rather break rock: stone and flint.

brushcutter.name: Brushcutter
brushcutter.text: Would rather gather brush and embers to keep the fire fed.

prospector.name: Prospector
prospector.text: Would rather dig ore: copper, cassiterite and bog iron.

warrior.name: Warrior
warrior.text: Patrols the settlement and fights anything that comes close. On quiet days half of them keep watch over gatherers working out past the houses, never straying far from home.

craftsperson.name: Craftsperson
craftsperson.text: Raises the buildings you order. Gathers wood when there is nothing to build, or lends a hand at a busy workshop.
